import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('/data/worldbank_education_gdp.csv')

# Identify the relevant columns
# Labor force participation rate (modeled ILO estimate)
labor_force_participation = df['Labor force participation rate, total (percentage of total population ages 15+) (modeled ILO estimate)']

# School enrollment, primary (percentage gross)
primary_enrollment = df['School enrollment, primary (percentage gross)']

# School enrollment, secondary (percentage gross)
secondary_enrollment = df['School enrollment, secondary (percentage gross)']

# Exports of goods and services (annual percentage growth)
export_growth = df['Exports of goods and services (annual percentage growth)']

# Combine the variables into a single DataFrame
data = pd.DataFrame({
    'LaborForce': labor_force_participation,
    'PrimaryEnrollment': primary_enrollment,
    'SecondaryEnrollment': secondary_enrollment,
    'ExportGrowth': export_growth
})

# Drop rows with missing values
data = data.dropna()

# Prepare the data for regression
X = data[['LaborForce', 'PrimaryEnrollment', 'SecondaryEnrollment']]
y = data['ExportGrowth']

# Create a linear regression model
model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(X, y)

# Get the coefficients
coefficients = model.coef_
coefficients

primary_enrollment_rows = df[df['Series Name'] == 'School enrollment, primary (percentage gross)']
secondary_enrollment_rows = df[df['Series Name'] == 'School enrollment, secondary (percentage gross)']
